clue.text: Trump his various victories

indicators.note: various suggests things in assorted forms, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A headline about a politician named Trump and his assorted wins.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram is almost exact: only the U and the I need to move, so the surface name points straight at the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Triumphs are great successes or wins, a direct plural synonym for victories.

clue.text: Subject for discussion after commencement of television series

indicators.note: commencement is the start, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: an issue is a topic being debated

explanation.surface: Talk of the start of a new television series as a topic for debate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the topic word after the single letter. A tissue of lies is a connected series of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tissue can mean an interwoven series or chain, as in a tissue of lies.

clue.text: Hostility shown by large company head

blocks.note: Imperial Chemical Industries, once a giant British firm

explanation.surface: Antagonism displayed by the boss of a big corporation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a chief executive but means a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour names like Sheerness. ICI was a major British chemical company.
explanation.definitionFit: Iciness is coldness of manner, an unfriendly frostiness close to hostility.

clue.text: Play short tune, hit by American originally

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the word loses its final letter
originally points to the origin, the opening letter of the word

blocks.note: a tune, cut by one letter here
to ram is to strike hard

explanation.surface: Perform a brief melody, a hit by an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' is the definition, the noun, though it reads as a verb in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A melodrama is a sensational stage drama, so it is a kind of play.

clue.text: Pompous drunk's fault, breaking in

indicators.note: breaking means smashing apart, so the word before it is reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A self-important drunk blames his breaking and entering.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Highfalutin is an informal word for pretentious or grandiloquent, so it matches pompous.

clue.text: Put an end to northerner attending church

blocks.note: a Scot comes from the north of Britain

explanation.surface: A Scotsman going to church brings something to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attending' here means sitting next to, so one piece simply follows the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a rumour or plan is to stop it decisively, to put an end to it.

clue.text: Clubs girl in form

blocks.note: C is the card abbreviation for clubs
a lass is a young woman

explanation.surface: A girl belonging to golf or social clubs is on top form.
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools a form is a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: A school form and a class are both groups of pupils taught together.

clue.text: Turtle avoiding soft piece of ground

indicators.note: avoiding means keeping away from, so that letter is left out

blocks.note: a terrapin is a freshwater turtle
p is piano, soft in musical notation

explanation.surface: A turtle steers clear of a soft patch of earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is land considered in terms of its physical features, a stretch or piece of ground.

clue.text: Deck conflagration? Hold back

blocks.note: to deck a room is to hang it with decorations

explanation.surface: A fire on a ship's deck, and the order to wait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' suggests a ship's floor, but here it is the verb to adorn, as in decking halls with hangings.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang fire is an idiom for delaying or holding back from acting.

clue.text: Stand motionless a long time

blocks.note: an age is a very long period

explanation.surface: An instruction to stand without moving for ages, like a sentry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand' reads as a verb but the definition is the noun: a stillage is a frame or platform for holding goods or barrels off the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A stillage is a supporting rack or platform, which is a kind of stand for casks or goods.

clue.text: A quicker route? Take a special turn by river

blocks.note: to rat is to change sides, a particular kind of turning against one's own party
a run is a small stream, especially in American usage

explanation.surface: Directions for a boat trip: make a particular turn beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: To rat is to desert or betray, so turning traitor is the 'special turn'. A rat run is a minor road drivers use as a shortcut to avoid traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat run is a back street that motorists use to bypass congestion, hence a quicker route, with the question mark flagging the loose fit.

clue.text: Overturn revolting object

blocks.note: people in revolt are said to be up in arms, or simply up
an end is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: Knock over some disgusting thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' looks like 'disgusting' but means rebelling, as in 'the people are up'.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend something is to turn it upside down, which is what overturning does.

clue.text: Pole tires on Welsh river

blocks.note: to flag is to grow weary

explanation.surface: A Polish person grows weary beside a Welsh river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a nationality but means a post. The Taff is the river running through Cardiff in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagstaff is the tall pole from which a flag is flown.

clue.text: Stuarts are assembled round top of historic Edinburgh landmark

indicators.note: assembled means put together, so the letters are fitted into a new order
round means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go around the other piece
top of a down entry's word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The Stuart kings gather around a historic Edinburgh site.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stuarts were Scotland's royal house, apt for an Edinburgh clue. Arthur's Seat is the extinct volcano overlooking the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur's Seat is the hill in Holyrood Park that dominates Edinburgh's skyline, a famous landmark there.

clue.text: Climber in brilliant red, one carrying a message

explanation.surface: A mountaineer dressed in bright red is a courier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer, but it is a climbing plant: the scarlet runner is a runner bean with red flowers, common in British gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarlet runner is a bean plant that climbs up poles and canes, so it is a climber.

clue.text: Disliked a French university cutting tree

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so one piece goes inside another

explanation.surface: A French college resented for felling a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' reads as felling the tree, but it means the university letter cuts into the tree's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpopular means not liked by many people, so disliked.

clue.text: Dogged English painter docked on about the third of March

indicators.note: docked means cut short, as a tail is, so the final letter goes
the third of points to the letter in third position of the next word
about means around, so one word wraps the selected letter

blocks.note: George Stubbs, the English painter of horses

explanation.surface: An English painter, persistent, cut short on around the third of March.
explanation.walkthrough: George Stubbs was the eighteenth-century English painter famous for horses; lose his final S, then put ON around the R.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogged and stubborn both describe refusing to give up or change course.

clue.text: Painting of distraught hapless putter

indicators.note: distraught means deeply upset, so the letters that follow are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A picture of an upset golfer who has just missed a putt.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf picture hides a famous artwork: Leonardo da Vinci's mural in Milan.
explanation.definitionFit: The Last Supper is Leonardo da Vinci's celebrated mural painting of Christ's final meal with the apostles.

clue.text: Solemn promise

blocks.note: second meaning: a pledge or token of what is to come

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it looks like a solemn vow; split, the word works as an adjective for seriousness and as a noun for a pledge, as in an earnest of good faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest as an adjective means grave and sincere; as a noun it is a token or guarantee of something to come.

clue.text: Managed to provoke endless bitterness

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: ran as in ran a business
to court trouble is to invite or provoke it

explanation.surface: Someone succeeded in stirring up lasting resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' here means to invite something unwelcome, as in courting disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is deep, long-lasting bitterness or resentment.

clue.text: Aviators crow, back on ground round centre of Ireland

indicators.note: ground means crushed up, so the preceding letters are broken and reshaped
round means placed around, so the rearranged letters enclose another
centre of picks the middle letter of the following word

blocks.note: the middle letter of the seven-letter word

explanation.surface: Pilots see a crow land back on the ground somewhere in central Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' in the enumeration is not clued. Alcock and Brown made the first non-stop transatlantic flight in 1919, crash-landing in a bog in Ireland, which the surface echoes.
explanation.definitionFit: John Alcock and Arthur Brown were the British aviators who first flew non-stop across the Atlantic.

clue.text: Essential facts given by bald doctor

blocks.note: Bones is slang for a doctor or surgeon, short for sawbones

explanation.surface: The key facts are supplied by a hairless physician.
explanation.walkthrough: Bones as a nickname for a doctor comes from 'sawbones', and was famously Dr McCoy's nickname in Star Trek.
explanation.definitionFit: The bare bones of something are its basic, essential elements, the core facts without detail.

clue.text: See 20
Severely criticise the Spanish jury

blocks.note: critics pan a show they dislike

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a Spanish jury for its verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel is a group of people chosen to judge or decide, as a jury is.

clue.text: Cat could be coolest when there's no sun

indicators.note: could be says the letters may become something else once rearranged
no sun means the letter abbreviating sun is taken away

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for sun, removed here

explanation.surface: A cat might be at its coolest once the sun has gone in.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the S from the seven letters leaves six, which rearrange into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a spotted wild cat of Central and South America.

clue.text: Rich source of oil furthermore includes diamonds

indicators.note: includes means one word holds another inside it

blocks.note: D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A wealthy person owns an oil well and diamonds too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rich' at the start is the whole definition; 'source of oil' must be read as one unit rather than part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-to-do is an idiom meaning prosperous or wealthy.

clue.text: Paying close attention to something out at golf

blocks.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Watching closely as something goes out of bounds on the golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Noting something means observing or remarking on it carefully.

clue.text: TV series to kick off on the subject of potassium

blocks.note: to begin, as a match kicks off
K is the chemical symbol for potassium

explanation.surface: A television series is about to start, on the topic of potassium.
explanation.definitionFit: Star Trek is the long-running science-fiction television series, an example of a TV series.
